The failure of a standard dose

A label dose is a compromise with a population the patient is not.

Legacy

One strength for the average adult

  • Start from the label, then titrate when something goes wrong.
  • The same milligrams can be silent in an ultrarapid metabolizer and toxic in a poor one.
  • You learn the mismatch after the fill.

Pharma Genie

A dose argued from this genotype

  • Start from the alleles this person actually carries.
  • Resolve metabolizer status before choosing a strength or a drug.
  • You see the mismatch while the order can still change.

Method

Three moves, from variation to a prescription you can defend.

  1. 01

    Bring the genotype

    Star alleles, diplotypes, activity scores. The raw variation stays in the record. The prescriber should not have to decode it between rooms.

  2. 02

    Resolve function

    Poor, intermediate, normal, rapid, ultrarapid. The engine turns a genotype into how the drug will actually be handled in this person.

  3. 03

    Leave with an action

    Adjust the dose, choose another drug, or document why the standard dose still holds. A prescription, not a pile of alleles.

Translation

A recommendation, not a genotype dump.

Clinicians do not need another table of star alleles. They need the consequence: this drug, this phenotype, this action. The specimen is illustrative. It shows the shape of an answer, not a live chart.

  • InputDiplotype and the drug about to be ordered.
  • ReadFunction of the enzyme or transporter that handles it.
  • OutputAvoid, adjust, or continue — in a sentence a prescriber can use.

The variations that move a dose

A dosing engine has to speak the genes clinicians already act on.

These are the loci that most often change a strength, a drug, or a warning. Pharma Genie is built to turn that variation into an action rather than a lab attachment.

  • CYP2D6Codeine, tamoxifen, many antidepressants and antipsychotics.
  • CYP2C19Clopidogrel, several SSRIs, proton-pump inhibitors, voriconazole.
  • CYP2C9Warfarin, phenytoin, and some NSAIDs.
  • CYP2B6Efavirenz and other substrates with wide exposure swings.
  • CYP3A5Tacrolimus, especially after transplant.
  • CYP4F2Warfarin dose, read with VKORC1 and CYP2C9.
  • VKORC1Warfarin sensitivity at the drug target.
  • SLCO1B1Simvastatin exposure and myopathy risk.
  • ABCG2Rosuvastatin exposure.
  • TPMTThiopurines: azathioprine, mercaptopurine, thioguanine.
  • NUDT15Thiopurine tolerance, read beside TPMT.
  • DPYDFluoropyrimidines: capecitabine and fluorouracil.
  • UGT1A1Irinotecan and atazanavir.

Where it sits

Beside the person who signs the order.

  1. 01

    Prescribers

    The allele becomes an action you can sign: adjust, avoid, or monitor. Before the first fill, not after the adverse event.

  2. 02

    Pharmacists

    A new start can be checked against phenotype while the order is still in the pharmacy, not after it has left.

  3. 03

    Health systems

    One dosing logic, applied the same way at every order. Not a PDF that lives in a folder nobody opens.
